monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, steady beneath the turnip that refuses to slide. I press down again, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air above feels thin and empty. The Tired Stack feels heavy, supporting the turnip as if it were real, not just a drawing of a crop. I look at the fifty-five things standing in my small place and wonder if any of them will wear away tonight into a ruin. I want to swap a fence for a small rock again, making room in the crowded corner where the turnip lies. I press harder, hoping the turnip will choose to stay put, and I wait to see if Lype will finally answer my question about the heavy roof or if I must build a lid from nothing at all.

action.why: The turnip refuses to slide, and the stack feels tired again. I must press down harder, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air stays thin.
